subject: Biology
central_question: How are the external organs of flowering plants described, modified, and represented systematically for identification and classification?
in_scope_units: Root systems, root functions, root regions, and tap, fibrous, and adventitious roots.
Stem origin, nodes, internodes, buds, functions, and modified roles.
Leaf parts, venation, simple and compound leaves, and phyllotaxy.
Flower organisation, sexuality, symmetry, floral merosity, ovary position, and floral whorls.
Calyx, corolla, aestivation, androecium, gynoecium, and placentation.
Fruit formation, pericarp, drupes, and parthenocarpy.
Semi-technical description, floral formula, and floral diagram.
Vegetative and floral characteristics and economic importance of Solanaceae.
banned_topics: Internal tissue anatomy of roots, stems, and leaves
Detailed physiology of photosynthesis and mineral absorption
Molecular mechanisms of fertilisation and seed development
Full taxonomic comparison of multiple flowering-plant families beyond Solanaceae

known_pitfalls.claim: Every underground plant part is a root.
known_pitfalls.correction: Underground stems can be identified by nodes, internodes, buds, and scale leaves; roots lack these stem characters.

known_pitfalls.claim: A leaflet of a compound leaf has an axillary bud.
known_pitfalls.correction: The axillary bud occurs at the base of the whole leaf's petiole, not at the base of each leaflet.

known_pitfalls.claim: Racemose and cymose refer to flower symmetry.
known_pitfalls.correction: They are inflorescence types distinguished by whether the main axis continues growing or ends in a flower.

known_pitfalls.claim: A superior ovary is positioned below all other floral parts.
known_pitfalls.correction: In a hypogynous flower the ovary is superior because other whorls arise below it.

known_pitfalls.claim: All fruits form only after fertilisation.
known_pitfalls.correction: Parthenocarpic fruits develop from the ovary without fertilisation.

known_pitfalls.claim: A monocot seed always lacks endosperm.
known_pitfalls.correction: Most monocot seeds are endospermic, though orchids are a stated exception.

recommended_example_progression: NCERT Exercises 1–2: compare compound leaves and explain alternate, opposite, and whorled phyllotaxy.
NCERT Exercises 3–4: define flower terms and differentiate racemose versus cymose and apocarpous versus syncarpous conditions.
NCERT Exercises 7–10: identify placentation, flower parts, inflorescences, and ovary position.
NCERT Exercise 5: label gram and maize seeds.
NCERT Exercise 6: prepare a semi-technical description and floral diagram of a Solanaceae flower.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: Use the end-of-chapter EXERCISES 1–10 for leaves, flower terminology, inflorescence, placentation, seeds, and Solanaceae.
